title: `ia validate` reports each `@execution-binding` as bound, unavailable or revoked against the catalog its host joined
summary: @inventarch/workspace-runtime adds the ./bind subpath (and ./internal/bind), exporting executionBindings(reader), executionBindingOf(record, resolve?) and bindExecution(binding, catalog) with the ExecutionBinding, BindingTarget, BindingCatalog, BindingResult and BindingStatus types; a present BindingCatalog's operation rows are @inventarch/db/distribution's InstalledOperation, the catalog's one shape. executionBindings reads every admitted `@execution-binding` in the root view, sorted by identity, with its unconditional binding.kind, binding.implementation and binding.target, a stated target kept as the reference written and the identity of the admitted record it resolves to (null when none answers it, and without a resolver), so a stated target is never read as no target. bindExecution returns bound only when the catalog is present, lists the implementation as available, the binding is of kind operation and its target, when it states one, resolves to the operation the implementation serves; unavailable when the binding names no implementation, its kind has no catalog section (only operation implementations are listed), the catalog is unavailable, does not list the implementation or lists it unavailable, the stated target resolves to no admitted record, or the implementation serves another operation; the canonical read-captured-source-binding therefore reports unavailable in an ia init consumer, which admits no `@operation` read-captured-source; and revoked, an error, when the catalog revokes the implementation or failed verification. @inventarch/distribution adds joinedCatalog(root, trust) with the JoinedCatalog type (a damaged one names the payload directory, whose deletion and a host re-apply are the repair) and the HostTrust type ({home, release}: the validating installation's IA home and the payload release it pins) and installationTrust(), the trust of the distribution module's own installation (the host payload it runs from, or null outside one). joinedCatalog opens only <home>/hosts/<release>: a join counts only when it and its host's registration name the pinned release and the registration names that payload directory, so a registration of another release or of a payload anywhere else (another IA home, inside the workspace, a network path) is unavailable with the repair ia host <host> --apply, and nothing it names is opened. It reads that payload once, reports it damaged when it fails verification with changed or unlisted files, a link, exceeded limits or a release.json that does not hash to the pin, parseable or not, whichever trusted join names it, takes the first trusted join in consumer order that carries its catalog digest, and is unavailable with the reasons when there is no receipt, no trust or no trusted join that holds (an ia project-only workspace, a host registered by another release, a drifted join, a payload without a catalog or not materialized); WorkspaceSession gains bindings(trust), with the ValidationBindings type, which returns that catalog source (null when the workspace has no binding, and then nothing beyond the records is read) and one result per binding, and ia-distribution validate, passing installationTrust(), adds it to its result as bindings and exits 1 when a binding is revoked. @inventarch/cli's ia validate reports the same bindings, trusting the payload its bundled host pin names in the IA home IA_HOME or IA_HOST_HOME resolves (or, run from inside a payload, that payload): --json adds bindings, and the human report adds a Bindings section with the catalog source and one row per binding, a summary line counting unbound bindings as not a pass, and revoked bindings as errors that fail the run and the closing line; a workspace with no binding keeps its human report unchanged. ia doctor's implementations row names a revoked operation and warns. Computing and reporting bindings writes nothing, in the workspace or the IA home. Limits: binding inspection and reporting do not load, import, serve or execute implementations. The separate local runner host binds and executes its fixed installed captured-read operation under the selected mandate and bounded runtime; only the catalog may revoke, since the `@execution-binding` schema has no revocation field; entry, hook and other non-operation bindings are always unavailable because the catalog lists no implementations of those kinds; a damaged joined payload revokes every operation binding, whatever implementation it names, while a missing payload file makes them unavailable; and ia validate's findings, counts, admission status and report outcome are unchanged, so a revoked binding fails the run without appearing among the findings.
